interactiveQuiz.question: Which router event fires immediately when a client-side route transition is triggered?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: routeChangeStart fires as soon as a user clicks a link or calls router.push().

sections.title: Q19: What is Shallow Routing in the Pages Router?
sections.content: Shallow routing allows changing the URL without re-running data fetching methods (`getStaticProps`, `getServerSideProps`). Call `router.push('/page?query=1', undefined, { shallow: true })` to update state in the URL while preserving active page component state.
keyTakeaways: Updates URL query string without re-triggering server data methods.
Only works for URL changes inside the **same page**.

codeExample.title: Executing Shallow Navigation
codeExample.explanation: Updates query parameter in the address bar without executing page data functions.

interactiveQuiz.question: Does shallow routing prevent getStaticProps/getServerSideProps from re-executing when navigating to a DIFFERENT page file?
options: Yes, shallow routing works globally across all pages
No, shallow routing only works for URL changes within the same active page component
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Shallow routing functions exclusively for state/query updates on the currently active page.

sections.title: Q20: When and why would you use a Custom Server (server.js) with Pages Router?
sections.content: A custom Node.js server (using Express or Fastify) was traditionally used to integrate custom backend routing or legacy HTTP proxies. **Warning**: Custom servers disable Automatic Static Optimization and cannot be deployed to serverless environments like Vercel.
keyTakeaways: Integrates custom Node.js frameworks (Express) with Next.js page rendering.
Disables Vercel serverless deployments and static optimization.

interactiveQuiz.question: What primary feature is lost when using a custom Express server.js file with Next.js?
options: Automatic Static Optimization and Serverless deployment compatibility
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Custom servers bypass Next.js default serverless builds and static optimization mechanisms.

sections.title: Q21: How do you trigger On-Demand ISR Revalidation in the Pages Router?
sections.content: On-Demand Revalidation purges static cache files immediately via an API route without waiting for the `revalidate` timer to expire. Call `res.revalidate('/target-page-path')` inside an authenticated API route handler.
keyTakeaways: Purges static page cache instantly on content updates.
Triggered via `res.revalidate('/path')` inside API routes.

codeExample.title: API Route Revalidation Handler
codeExample.explanation: res.revalidate immediately rebuilds the target static page cache.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which response method triggers On-Demand Revalidation inside a Pages Router API route?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: res.revalidate('/path') purges and regenerates the specified static HTML path on demand.

sections.title: Q22: How does next/dynamic perform code splitting in the Pages Router?
sections.content: `next/dynamic` wraps standard `import()` calls to lazy-load React components, splitting them into separate JS chunks. Setting `{ ssr: false }` skips server-side rendering for browser-only libraries.
keyTakeaways: Reduces initial bundle size by lazy-loading components on demand.
Use `{ ssr: false }` for browser-dependent modules.

codeExample.title: Lazy Loading Component with next/dynamic
codeExample.explanation: HeavyChart is split into an independent JS chunk and rendered exclusively on the client.

interactiveQuiz.question: What parameter setting in next/dynamic prevents a heavy client chart library from rendering on Node.js servers?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: ssr: false skips server-side rendering execution for client-bound modules.

sections.title: Q23: What was Preview Mode in the Pages Router and how was it enabled?
sections.content: Preview Mode bypassed static pre-rendering (SSG) to fetch draft content from Headless CMSs. Enabled by an API route calling `res.setPreviewData({})`, which set preview cookies that forced `getStaticProps` to render dynamically at request time.
keyTakeaways: Bypasses SSG build cache to show unpublished draft content.
Enabled via `res.setPreviewData({})` inside API routes.

interactiveQuiz.question: How does Pages Router Preview Mode signal getStaticProps to render draft content dynamically?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: res.setPreviewData() sets HTTP cookies that instruct Next.js to run getStaticProps dynamically per request.

sections.title: Q24: How do you implement persistent Page-Level Layouts in the Pages Router?
sections.content: Attach a custom `.getLayout` function property to individual page components. In `pages/_app.js`, execute `Component.getLayout()` to wrap active pages without unmounting shared layouts during navigation.
keyTakeaways: Attaches custom `.getLayout` properties to page component functions.
Preserves component state and scroll position across page transitions.

codeExample.title: Page-Level Layout Setup
codeExample.explanation: _app.js executes the page's getLayout function to maintain layout tree persistence.

interactiveQuiz.question: What advantage does the getLayout pattern offer over wrapping page JSX directly in a layout component inside each file?
options: Persists layout state and DOM nodes across route changes without re-mounting shared layouts
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Executing getLayout in _app.js keeps shared layout components mounted across route changes, preserving state.

sections.title: Q25: How do you extend Webpack configuration inside next.config.js for the Pages Router?
sections.content: Custom Webpack configurations are defined inside the `webpack` property in `next.config.js`. It receives the existing `config` object and options (`isServer`, `dev`, `webpack`) to mutate or append plugins.
keyTakeaways: Extend Webpack rules using `next.config.js`.
Check `options.isServer` to target server vs client bundle configurations.

codeExample.title: Extending Webpack in next.config.js
codeExample.explanation: Modifies resolution fallbacks to prevent bundling Node modules into client bundles.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which flag inside next.config.js webpack options determines if Webpack is bundling server code?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: options.isServer evaluates to true when Webpack builds the server-side bundle.

sections.title: Q26: What properties are available on the context parameter in getStaticProps?
sections.content: The `context` parameter in `getStaticProps` provides keys: `params` (dynamic path parameters), `preview` (boolean for preview mode), `previewData`, `locale`, `locales`, and `defaultLocale`.
keyTakeaways: `params` contains dynamic URL route parameters.
Contains localization and preview mode metadata.

interactiveQuiz.question: Is req (the HTTP Request object) available inside getStaticProps context?
options: No, because getStaticProps executes at build time when no user HTTP request exists
interactiveQuiz.explanation: getStaticProps runs at build time, meaning no user HTTP request (req) object exists.

sections.title: Q27: What properties are available on the context parameter in getServerSideProps?
sections.content: `getServerSideProps` context includes: `req` (HTTP IncomingMessage), `res` (HTTP ServerResponse), `query` (URL query string and path params), `params`, `resolvedUrl`, `locale`, `locales`, and `defaultLocale`.
keyTakeaways: Provides direct access to Node.js HTTP `req` and `res` objects.
`query` contains both query string parameters and path parameters.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which object in getServerSideProps context allows reading client request cookies?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Client cookies are transmitted in HTTP headers, accessed via context.req.

sections.title: Q28: How does Internationalized (i18n) Routing work in the Pages Router?
sections.content: Next.js provides built-in internationalized routing configured in `next.config.js`. Supports two strategies: **Sub-path Routing** (`/en/blog`, `/fr/blog`) and **Domain Routing** (`example.com/blog`, `example.fr/blog`).
keyTakeaways: Configure `i18n` object in `next.config.js` with `locales` and `defaultLocale`.
Access active locale via `useRouter().locale` or `context.locale`.

codeExample.title: i18n Configuration
codeExample.explanation: Automatically handles sub-path localization routing across all pages.

interactiveQuiz.question: How do you access the active locale string inside getStaticProps?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: context.locale provides the active locale string inside server data fetching methods.

sections.title: Q29: How do you trigger server-side redirects inside getStaticProps or getServerSideProps?
sections.content: Return a `redirect` object from `getStaticProps` or `getServerSideProps` containing `destination` (string) and `permanent` (boolean: `true` for 308, `false` for 307) or `statusCode`.
keyTakeaways: Return `{ redirect: { destination: '/login', permanent: false } }`.
Halts page rendering and issues an immediate HTTP redirect response.

codeExample.title: Server-Side Redirect in getServerSideProps
codeExample.explanation: Unauthenticated requests are redirected server-side before page rendering occurs.

interactiveQuiz.question: What status code is returned when setting permanent: false inside a server redirect object?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: permanent: false issues a temporary redirect (307 Temporary Redirect).

sections.title: Q30: How do you return a 404 response from getStaticProps or getServerSideProps?
sections.content: Return `{ notFound: true }` from `getStaticProps` or `getServerSideProps`. Next.js immediately stops page rendering and serves the custom `pages/404.js` page with a 404 HTTP status code.
keyTakeaways: Return `{ notFound: true }` when target database items do not exist.
Renders the custom 404 error page automatically.

codeExample.title: Returning 404 for Missing Database Records
codeExample.explanation: If fetchPost returns null, notFound: true renders the 404 error page.

interactiveQuiz.question: What happens when getStaticProps returns { notFound: true }?
options: App throws an uncaught JavaScript error
Next.js returns an HTTP 404 status and renders pages/404.js
Renders the page with empty props
interactiveQuiz.explanation: returning { notFound: true } instructs Next.js to serve the 404 page and return a 404 status.

sections.title: Q31: How does next/script manage third-party script loading in the Pages Router?
sections.content: The `next/script` component optimizes third-party JS execution timing via strategies: `beforeInteractive` (injected in head before hydration), `afterInteractive` (default, loaded after page hydration), and `lazyOnload` (loaded during idle time).
keyTakeaways: Controls third-party script execution timing.
Prevents third-party scripts from blocking initial page rendering.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which strategy in next/script should be used for critical analytics or bot detection scripts that must execute before page hydration?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: beforeInteractive injects scripts into the initial server HTML head so they run before main hydration scripts.

sections.title: Q32: How do you disable the default body parser in Pages Router API routes?
sections.content: Export a `config` object from the API route file with `api: { bodyParser: false }`. Disabling body parsing is necessary when processing raw file streams, file uploads (e.g. using `multer` or `formidable`), or verifying raw webhooks (like Stripe).
keyTakeaways: Export `export const config = { api: { bodyParser: false } }`.
Required for raw request body stream processing.

codeExample.title: Disabling Body Parser for Webhooks
codeExample.explanation: Disabling bodyParser grants direct access to the unparsed HTTP request stream.

interactiveQuiz.question: Why must you set bodyParser: false when receiving raw Stripe webhook events in an API route?
options: Signature verification requires the exact unparsed raw binary/string request body
Next.js does not support JSON bodies
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Cryptographic webhook signatures require calculating hashes over the raw unparsed request body.

sections.title: Q33: How do CSS Modules work in the Pages Router?
sections.content: Next.js supports CSS Modules out of the box using the `.module.css` extension. Styles defined inside CSS modules are scoped locally to the importing component file to avoid global class name collisions.
keyTakeaways: Use `[name].module.css` files.
Automatically generates unique scoped CSS class names.

codeExample.title: Importing CSS Modules
codeExample.explanation: styles.btnPrimary resolves to a unique scoped class name string like Button_btnPrimary__1a2b3.

interactiveQuiz.question: Where can global un-scoped CSS stylesheets (e.g., import '../styles/global.css') be imported in the Pages Router?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: To prevent global CSS specificity conflicts, global stylesheets can only be imported in pages/_app.js.

sections.title: Q34: How does client-side navigation work using next/link in the Pages Router?
sections.content: The `<Link href="...">` component performs client-side transitions using HTML5 History APIs without triggering full browser page reloads. When a Link enters the browser viewport, Next.js automatically **prefetches** the page's JS bundle and JSON data in the background.
keyTakeaways: Enables fast SPA navigation without full page reloads.
Automatically prefetches linked page assets when scrolled into the viewport.

interactiveQuiz.question: What asset does Next.js prefetch when a <Link href="/about"> enters the viewport for an SSG page?
options: The page's compiled JavaScript bundle and static JSON props data file
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Next.js prefetches the JS component bundle and JSON props payload to enable instant client-side rendering upon click.

sections.title: Q35: How are Environment Variables handled in the Pages Router?
sections.content: Environment variables defined in `.env.local` are private to the server runtime by default. To expose environment variables to the browser client, prefix their names with `NEXT_PUBLIC_` (e.g. `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`).
keyTakeaways: Server-only by default (`process.env.DB_PASS`).
Prefix with `NEXT_PUBLIC_` to inline variables into client JavaScript bundles.

codeExample.title: Accessing Environment Variables
codeExample.explanation: NEXT_PUBLIC_ variables are replaced with their inline literal values during build compilation.

interactiveQuiz.question: What happens if you reference process.env.SECRET_KEY (without NEXT_PUBLIC_) inside a client React component function?
options: It evaluates to undefined on the client to prevent security leaks
It exposes the key in the client JavaScript bundle
It prompts the user for a password
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Variables lacking NEXT_PUBLIC_ are omitted from client bundles, resolving to undefined in browser scripts.

sections.title: Q36: How do you attach custom HTTP response headers to pages in the Pages Router?
sections.content: Custom response headers can be set globally in `next.config.js` via the `headers()` async function, or per-request inside `getServerSideProps` using `context.res.setHeader('Header-Name', 'Value')`.
keyTakeaways: Global headers: Configure `headers()` in `next.config.js`.
Dynamic headers: Call `context.res.setHeader()` in `getServerSideProps`.

codeExample.title: Setting Headers in getServerSideProps
codeExample.explanation: Sets custom HTTP Cache-Control headers directly on the Node.js response object.

interactiveQuiz.question: Can you call context.res.setHeader() inside getStaticProps?
options: No, because getStaticProps runs at build time and does not process individual HTTP response objects
interactiveQuiz.explanation: getStaticProps runs at build time when no active HTTP server response (res) exists.

sections.title: Q37: How do you structure pages/_app.js if you MUST use getInitialProps?
sections.content: If `_app.js` uses `getInitialProps`, you must manually execute `App.getInitialProps(appContext)` and spread `appProps.pageProps` to preserve page-level data fetching.
keyTakeaways: Must execute `App.getInitialProps(appContext)` explicitly.
Opt-out of static optimization globally across all pages.

codeExample.title: Custom App getInitialProps Pattern
codeExample.explanation: Executes framework App.getInitialProps to gather pageProps for the active component.

interactiveQuiz.question: What is the recommended modern alternative to adding global data fetching in pages/_app.js with getInitialProps?
options: Use React Context or SWR/React Query for client-side data fetching where needed
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Fetching global client state with SWR/React Query preserves static optimization for individual pages.

sections.title: Q38: How does trailingSlash configuration affect Pages Router routing?
sections.content: Setting `trailingSlash: true` in `next.config.js` redirects URLs without trailing slashes to their trailing slash equivalent (`/about` -> `/about/`). Static export builds output `about/index.html` instead of `about.html`.
keyTakeaways: Configured via `trailingSlash: true` in `next.config.js`.
Shapes static export HTML folder structures.

interactiveQuiz.question: When trailingSlash: true is configured, what HTML file path is generated for pages/contact.js during static export?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: trailingSlash: true generates subfolder index files (contact/index.html) to match trailing slash directory URLs.

sections.title: Q39: How did Accelerated Mobile Pages (AMP) work in the Pages Router?
sections.content: The Pages Router supported AMP via `export const config = { amp: true }` (pure AMP) or `amp: 'hybrid'` (serves both standard HTML and AMP routes like `/page?amp=1`). Use `useAmp()` hook to inspect rendering mode.
keyTakeaways: Configured via `export const config = { amp: true | 'hybrid' }`.
Note: AMP support is legacy and removed in modern App Router setups.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which hook in the Pages Router determined if a component was currently rendering in AMP mode for hybrid AMP pages?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: useAmp() returned true when rendering the AMP version of a hybrid page.

sections.title: Q40: What was target: 'serverless' in legacy Next.js Pages Router builds?
sections.content: Legacy Next.js builds offered `target: 'serverless'`, compiling every page inside `pages/` into an independent self-contained Node.js Lambda function rather than a single monolithic server instance. (Deprecated in modern versions in favor of automatic Vercel serverless splitting).
keyTakeaways: Compiled individual pages into standalone isolated Lambda functions.
Replaced by modern automatic serverless platform slicing.

interactiveQuiz.question: Why was target: 'serverless' historically useful for cloud deployments?
options: It split pages into isolated functions so scaling one page didn't require scaling the entire monolithic app
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Isolated serverless functions allowed granular scaling and independent cold-start execution per route.

sections.title: Q41: How does the basePath configuration option work in next.config.js?
sections.content: `basePath: '/docs'` hosting allows serving a Next.js application under a URL sub-path instead of root domain paths. All `<Link>` components and asset paths automatically prepend the specified basePath prefix.
keyTakeaways: Configured via `basePath: '/prefix'` in `next.config.js`.
Prefixes all routes and internal links automatically.

codeExample.title: Setting basePath in next.config.js
codeExample.explanation: Pages in pages/about.js are automatically served from /sub-app/about.

interactiveQuiz.question: If basePath: '/portal' is set, what URL corresponds to pages/settings.js?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: basePath automatically prepends /portal to all route paths.

sections.title: Q42: What is the route specificity matching priority in the Pages Router?
sections.content:
When URL paths match multiple route patterns, Next.js evaluates route priority in strict order:
1. **Predefined explicit routes** (`pages/post/create.js`)
2. **Dynamic routes** (`pages/post/[id].js`)
3. **Catch-all routes** (`pages/post/[...slug].js`) 
4. **Optional Catch-all routes** (`pages/post/[[...slug]].js`)
keyTakeaways: Explicit static route files take precedence over dynamic wildcard files.
Optional catch-all files have the lowest specificity priority.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which page file handles the incoming URL /posts/new if both pages/posts/new.js and pages/posts/[id].js exist?
options: Next.js throws a route collision error
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Explicit predefined route files (new.js) always take precedence over dynamic parameter routes ([id].js).

sections.title: Q43: How is SWR used for client-side data fetching alongside SSG in Pages Router?
sections.content: A common pattern combines SSG for initial skeleton HTML with SWR (`useSWR`) on the client for live data revalidation. Initial static data can be passed to SWR as `fallbackData` inside `getStaticProps`.
keyTakeaways: Combines static page pre-rendering with dynamic client-side hydration.
Pass initial props to SWR's `fallbackData` option.

codeExample.title: Combining SSG with Client SWR Revalidation
codeExample.explanation: Pre-renders initialData statically at build time, while useSWR polls for live client-side updates.

interactiveQuiz.question: What role does fallbackData play when passing getStaticProps data into the useSWR hook?
options: Provides initial data for rendering before client-side fetching completes
interactiveQuiz.explanation: fallbackData populates SWR initial state instantly with server pre-rendered data during client hydration.

sections.title: Q44: How do you configure SVG inline loading in Pages Router next.config.js using @svgr/webpack?
sections.content: To import SVG files directly as React components in the Pages Router, extend `next.config.js` with Webpack module rules targeting `@svgr/webpack`.
keyTakeaways: Extends Webpack module rules for custom file extensions.
Allows importing `.svg` files directly as React component functions.

codeExample.title: SVGR Webpack Config
codeExample.explanation: Allows writing import Logo from './logo.svg' and rendering <Logo /> directly in JSX.

interactiveQuiz.question: Where do you append custom file transformation loaders in a Next.js application?
options: Inside the webpack function in next.config.js
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Webpack loader rules are added to config.module.rules within next.config.js.

sections.title: Q45: Can the pages/ directory and app/ directory coexist in the same Next.js project?
sections.content: Yes! Next.js supports incremental migration. The `pages/` directory and `app/` directory can coexist in the same codebase. Routes defined in `app/` take priority over identical paths in `pages/`.
keyTakeaways: Supports step-by-step incremental migration.
`app/` directory routes take precedence over matching `pages/` routes.

interactiveQuiz.question: If both pages/about.js and app/about/page.js exist in the same codebase, which file renders when navigating to /about?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: App Router routes take precedence over matching Pages Router paths during incremental migration.

sections.title: Q46: How do you migrate a Pages Router component with getServerSideProps to the App Router?
sections.content: In the App Router, delete `getServerSideProps`. Convert the page component into an `async` Server Component, and call dynamic `fetch('...', { cache: 'no-store' })` or query databases directly inside the component body.
keyTakeaways: Replace `getServerSideProps` with direct async calls inside React Server Components.
Use `{ cache: 'no-store' }` or dynamic functions (`cookies()`, `headers()`) to force request-time rendering.

codeExample.title: Migration Example
codeExample.explanation: App Router eliminates getServerSideProps wrapper code in favor of async Server Components.

interactiveQuiz.question: What replaces getServerSideProps when migrating a page to an App Router Server Component?
options: Direct async fetch/database calls inside the Server Component body
interactiveQuiz.explanation: React Server Components run asynchronously on the server, executing data fetching directly inside the component function body.

sections.title: Q47: How do you migrate getStaticProps and getStaticPaths to the App Router?
sections.content:
- `getStaticProps`: Replaced by standard `fetch()` calls inside Server Components (which cache by default or using `{ cache: 'force-cache' }`).
- `getStaticPaths`: Replaced by `export async function generateStaticParams()`.
keyTakeaways: `getStaticProps` -> native cached `fetch()` calls inside Server Components.
`getStaticPaths` -> `generateStaticParams()`.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which function replaces getStaticPaths when migrating a dynamic route to the App Router?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: generateStaticParams outputs route parameters for dynamic route pre-rendering in the App Router.

sections.title: Q48: How do you prevent a component from rendering during SSR in the Pages Router?
sections.content:
To render a component exclusively on the client in the Pages Router:
1. Wrap import with `next/dynamic(() => import(...), { ssr: false })`.
2. Or check `typeof window !== 'undefined'` / wrap render in a `useEffect` mounted state check.
keyTakeaways: Use `next/dynamic` with `{ ssr: false }`.
Prevents hydration errors for window/document dependent libraries.

codeExample.title: Mounted Effect Pattern for Client-Only Rendering
codeExample.explanation: useEffect fires exclusively on the client after mount, preventing server pre-rendering of children.

interactiveQuiz.question: Why does evaluating window.innerWidth directly inside a component's render body cause a hydration mismatch error?
options: Because window is undefined during server pre-rendering, producing mismatched server and client HTML markup
Because window is a React keyword
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Server rendering lacks window objects; accessing them directly creates mismatching HTML structures during client hydration.

sections.title: Q49: How do you enable Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) in Pages Router API routes?
sections.content: To enable CORS in an API route, attach standard CORS response headers (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, `Access-Control-Allow-Methods`) directly using `res.setHeader()`, or wrap the handler using the `cors` npm package.
keyTakeaways: Set `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` using `res.setHeader()`.
Handle HTTP `OPTIONS` preflight requests explicitly.

codeExample.title: CORS Headers in API Route
codeExample.explanation: Responds to OPTIONS preflight checks and sets origin headers to permit cross-site requests.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which HTTP request method must be handled to respond to browser CORS preflight checks inside an API route handler?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Browsers automatically send an HTTP OPTIONS request prior to cross-origin requests to verify permission headers.

sections.title: Q50: What are the main architectural tradeoffs of the Pages Router compared to the App Router?
sections.content:
- **Pages Router Strengths**: Simple mental model, proven stability, straightforward page-level data methods (`getStaticProps`/`getServerSideProps`), extensive legacy ecosystem support.
- **Pages Router Tradeoffs**: Larger client JS bundle sizes (no React Server Components), rigid page-level layout constraints (lacks nested layout tree persistence), coarse request-time data fetching granularities.
keyTakeaways: Pages Router: Page-centric rendering with mandatory client hydration.
App Router: Component-centric rendering powered by React Server Components and nested layouts.

interactiveQuiz.question: What primary React capability is available natively in the App Router but absent in the Pages Router architecture?
options: React Server Components (RSC) and nested persistence layouts
interactiveQuiz.explanation: The App Router is built on React Server Components and nested layout trees, capabilities absent from the Pages Router.
